objectives: Say what Allah made Adam from.
Understand made, took, told and came.
Say why people have different skin colors.
content.pedagogy: Grammar is found in the story first. Learners notice the form in a story sentence, then use it about their own life. With young learners (Years 2–4), teach the Language Focus as chunks: say, repeat, act and play.
content.grammarFocus: Past forms in a story (made, took, told, came, was).
content.pronunciationFocus: AN-gel; EARTH (the th sounds like in “think”).
content.lessonPlan: 0–5 Show a little soil in a cup. Ask: “What is this? What grows in it?” 5–10 Listen once with one question: “What did Allah make the first human from?” 10–17 Read. Learners underline made, took and told. 17–20 Quick Challenge. 20–27 Language Focus 1–2 on the board: “make → made”. 27–30 Say It in pairs. The audio for A1 is not ready yet: read the chapter aloud yourself, slowly, twice.
discussionPoints: People have different skin colors. We are all Adam’s children. What does this teach us?
interactiveTips: Tap the two hotspots on the picture before the Quick Challenge.
Word Notes: earth, angel, surprised, soil.

differentiation.strugglingLearners: Give the three sentence frames on a strip.
differentiation.fastFinishers: Learners add one more sentence: “We are all his children.”

checkQuestions: How many verbs do you underline? (three)
classroomManagement.monitoring: Listen for made and took, not “maked” or “taked”. Check that learners say “angels”, not “angles”.

rubricLevels.secure: Uses made, took and told correctly.
rubricLevels.notYet: Play make → made ping-pong for two minutes.
Give two picture cards: soil and people.

objectives: Say why Iblis did not show respect.

content.pedagogy: Grammar is found in the story first. Learners notice the form in a story sentence, then use it about their own life. With young learners (Years 2–4), teach the Language Focus as chunks: say, repeat, act and play.
content.grammarFocus: Could + verb; past negative with did not (EGP: did not is A2, so learners find and choose it; free use is not expected).
content.lessonPlan: 0–5 Ask: “What could you do when you were a baby?” 5–10 Listen: “Who did not show respect?” 10–17 Read. Two columns on the board: “did” / “did not”. 17–20 Quick Challenge. 20–27 Language Focus. 27–30 Say It: “When I was five, I could …” The audio for A1 is not ready yet: read the chapter aloud yourself, slowly, twice.

metadata.title: Prophet Adam (pbuh) A1 — Teacher Guide
metadata.subtitle: 8 short lessons with chapter-specific support, grammar found in the story, and 30-minute lesson plans
metadata.estimatedDuration: 8 chapter lessons of about 30 minutes each, plus one 40-minute review lesson for the end pages.
metadata.targetAudience: A1 English learners: young beginners (Years 2–4) and adult beginners.
metadata.targetLearners: Learners who can read very short, simple sentences with pictures, sentence frames and help from the teacher.
metadata.purpose: Develop A1 reading, listening, speaking and writing through the story of Prophet Adam (pbuh), Iblis, Paradise, life on the earth and the two brothers.
metadata.approachDesc: Route in every chapter: Before You Read → Listen → Read → Quick Challenge → Language Focus (Look → Practise → Use) → I can. Grammar is found in the story first. Learners notice the form in a story sentence, then use it about their own life.

readingFramework.before: Before You Read: one picture or one guess question.
readingFramework.during: The audio for A1 is not ready yet: read the chapter aloud yourself, slowly, twice. Then learners read and do one small task (underline, columns, act).
readingFramework.after: Quick Challenge, then Language Focus (Look → Practise → Use), then I can and an exit ticket.

cefrProfile.intro: This book is written for CEFR A1. The table shows the A1 descriptors of the CEFR Companion Volume (2020) that the tasks are built on. Vocabulary (English Vocabulary Profile): learners see only A1 words, words with a Word Note and words from the story. Instruction words that the app uses in every book (match, order, true, false, chapter) are taught once in the first lesson. Grammar (English Grammar Profile): past simple affirmative, was / were, could, because, always and there is / there are are A1. Did not, never and imperatives are A2. The story uses them, so learners meet them in the text and choose them in exercises. Free use is only expected with sentence frames. Türkiye Century Maarif Model English Curriculum (Years 2–8): “CEFR level A1 has been adapted as A1.1, A1.2, A1.3 in Years 2, 3 and 4 for Primary Education.” The grammar route follows the Year 4 (Level A1.3) “Target Language Chunks in Use”: “To be” in the past (was, were), “There was/ There were”, “The Simple Past Tense (+) (-) (?)” with regular and irregular verbs, and wh- question words. Imperatives are in Year 2, Theme 1. The curriculum’s learning outcomes are written for its own themes. This book is a supplementary reader, so it supports these language chunks but does not cover a theme’s outcomes. Young learners (Years 2–4): the curriculum says “There is no analysis or teaching of grammatical structures at this stage.” With children, teach each Language Focus as chunks: say, repeat, act and play. Do not read the Explanation lines to them. The Explanation lines are for adult beginners and for self-study.

rows.descriptor: Can understand very short, simple texts a single phrase at a time, picking up familiar names, words and basic phrases and rereading as required.
practice: Before You Read and Quick Challenge in every chapter.

rows.descriptor: Can ask and answer simple questions, initiate and respond to simple statements in areas of immediate need or on very familiar topics.
practice: Chapter 2: ask and answer “What could you do when you were five?”

rows.descriptor: Can produce simple, mainly isolated phrases about people and places.
practice: Chapter 5: say how you helped at home.

rows.descriptor: Can give information about matters of personal relevance (e.g. likes and dislikes, family, pets) using simple words/signs and basic expressions. Can produce simple isolated phrases and sentences.
practice: Chapter 3: write about a beautiful place.

rows.descriptor: Can understand instructions addressed carefully and slowly to them and follow short, simple directions.
practice: Instruction check questions in every chapter (Classroom management).

sensitiveNotes.title: Source fidelity and respectful teaching
notes: Never draw or show Prophet Adam (pbuh), Eve or any prophet. Use places, objects and the pictures in the app only.
Chapters 6 and 7 tell of Qabil and Habil. Keep the talk calm: do not act out anger or the death, and keep the focus on the lessons (no jealousy, stop your anger).
Do not add legends, dates or details that are not in this A1 book.

grammarSequence: Chapter 1: Past forms in a story (made, took, told, came, was).
Chapter 2: Could + verb; past negative with did not (EGP: did not is A2, so learners find and choose it; free use is not expected).
Chapter 3: was / were; imperatives: Do not go, Be careful (EGP: imperatives are A2, so learners understand them in the story).
Chapter 4: Irregular past forms (ate, forgot, knew, forgave); always and never before the verb (EGP: never is A2; use it with the frames).
Chapter 5: Regular past -ed (worked, looked after, helped, wanted) next to irregular forms (grew, had, made, taught).
Chapter 6: because for reasons; will not + verb in Habil’s words.
Chapter 7: Past forms: felt, sent (change); learned, cried, watched (-ed; cry → cried).
Chapter 8: Imperatives for advice: Love Allah, Be kind, Do not be jealous.
